findings.summary: Custom type parser only intercepts scalar DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ oids, not their array oids (_date=1182, _timestamp=1115, _timestamptz=1185), so array-of-date/timestamp columns still go through pg's default array parser and are returned as JS Date objects, reintroducing the exact timezone-shift bug this change is meant to fix for those columns.
findings.evidence: RAW_TEXT_OIDS only contains types.builtins.DATE, TIMESTAMP, TIMESTAMPTZ (scalar oids). datasourceTypeParser checks RAW_TEXT_OIDS.has(oid) using the queried column's dataTypeID directly; for an array column the oid is the array type's own oid (e.g. 1182 for _date), which is not in the set, so getDefaultParser is used and pg-types' built-in array parser converts each element to a Date via its own internal per-element parsing, bypassing the raw-text override.

findings.summary: executeQuery now issues two additional SET statements (TimeZone, DateStyle) after the existing statement_timeout SET, each awaited individually with no transaction; if a managed/restricted Postgres instance disallows changing DateStyle or TimeZone at session level (e.g. via certain proxy/pooler configurations), executeQuery will throw for all queries against that datasource where it previously worked, since these SETs are unconditionally required before the wrapped query runs.
findings.evidence: await client.query(`SET TimeZone = 'UTC'`); await client.query(`SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'`); — added unconditionally in the same try block as the main query, so any failure here (e.g., due to a restrictive connection pooler or permissions setup) surfaces as a full query failure rather than being handled gracefully.

findings.summary: New `toCell` Date-handling branch is never exercised by any test
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:29-33 adds `if (val instanceof Date) return val.toISOString();` as new behavior, and the datasource.service.ts change (RAW_TEXT_OIDS overriding DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ to raw strings) means the only OIDs pg would otherwise parse into a JS `Date` are exactly the ones now intercepted to stay as strings. So no query result value flowing through toCell in the e2e suite (packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts) is ever an actual `Date` instance, and there is no dedicated unit test for readonly.ts/toCell in packages/sheets (no *.spec.ts/*.test.ts found under packages/sheets/src/store). findings.summary: Existing precise row-equality assertions were weakened to loose String() coercion checks without any behavior justification
findings.evidence: packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts:85 and :112 (and the analogous ownership test) changed `expect(rows).toEqual([{ n: 1 }])` to `expect(String(rows[0].n)).toBe('1')`. The `n` column is INT4, which is unaffected by the new type-parser change (only DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ are overridden), so there is no reason for this test to stop checking the actual returned type/value; the loosened assertion would also pass if `rows[0].n` regressed to the string `'1'` instead of the number `1`, silently losing coverage of int4 decoding.

verdict.reason: toCell's Date branch (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:32-36, `if (val instanceof Date) return val.toISOString();`) is exercised nowhere with an actual Date instance. Repo-wide grep for `toCell` shows only two call sites: readonly.ts itself and packages/backend/test/database.e2e-spec.ts (lines 175, 301). That e2e test drives values through DataSourceService.executeQuery, which installs a custom pg type parser (datasource.service.ts:21-37) that forces DATE, TIMESTAMP, and TIMESTAMPTZ — exactly the three OIDs pg's default parser turns into JS `Date` objects — to be returned as raw strings via `RAW_TEXT_OIDS`. The typeMap in the e2e 'all pg built-in types' test confirms this: DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ expected cell values are plain date/time strings (e.g. '2025-06-15', '2025-06-15 14:30:00'), not `.toISOString()` output, meaning no Date instance ever reaches `toCell` there. I searched for any other test path: `glob **/*.spec.ts` and `**/*.test.ts` under packages/sheets (52 files) show no store/readonly test file; grep for `ReadOnlyStore`/`loadQueryResults` across the repo finds only source (readonly.ts, sheets/index.ts) and frontend production usage (datasource-view.tsx) — no test file calls loadQueryResults or constructs a ReadOnlyStore with Date values; grep for `new Date(` in database.e2e-spec.ts finds only one unrelated usage (share-link expiry, line 462), not near toCell calls. I found no counterexample after this broad search, so the absence claim stands.

verdict.reason:
The finding conflates a narrow backend correctness fix with an "architecture-level change to Query Execution" that supposedly requires a design-doc update and contradicts the doc's stated limitation. Reading the actual code (datasource.service.ts:19-37, 142-145, 196-205) shows the RAW_TEXT_OIDS/getTypeParser override exists purely to stop node-postgres from auto-converting DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ columns into JS Date objects that get shifted by the server's local timezone (per the code comment at lines 19-20: "Keep date/time types as raw Postgres text instead of JS Date, which the default parser shifts by the Node runtime timezone"), and the SET TimeZone/SET DateStyle calls simply make that raw-text output deterministic (UTC, ISO format). This is a bug fix for value-serialization consistency, not a feature that maps PostgreSQL types to spreadsheet cell formats. Confirming this: the frontend (datasource.ts:18, datasource-view.tsx:108) still only carries dataTypeID as inert metadata and performs no type-aware cell formatting (no numbers/dates/booleans distinction) - so the doc's Current Limitation #9 ("No column type mapping - All values are displayed as strings regardless of the PostgreSQL data type", line 205) and Medium-term Next Step "Column type awareness" (line 221) remain accurate and are not contradicted; the doc is stale on an implementation detail but not self-contradictory on the architectural claim it makes. Under the design-fit rubric, design-doc discipline is scoped to architecture/data-model changes; a type-parser tweak to avoid timezone bugs in raw value passthrough is implementation/correctness-level work (this lens explicitly defers line-level logic bugs), not an architecture change requiring a design-doc update.</parameter>
